title: Chilton on Lester's 1933-36 career: Henderson, Kirk and Basie
summary: Phillips says Lester stayed with King Oliver from spring until November 1933, then went to Basie; Dupre reads Chilton's account of Little Rock, Henderson, Boyd Atkins and Basie's Reno Club.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Chilton doesn't mention King. It just says, "Worked with various territory bands before settling in Chicago."
He ain't in Chicago. He's in San Francisco.
It says "He settled in California in the mid-1940's." This is in the 1930's, in Chicago. Anyway, Lester Young joined the band at what time? In the spring of 1933, you were saying?

Yeah, it was the spring. Must have been round about April, May, somewhere along in there. And he came in the band and he stayed in the band until November. He stayed with King until November. That's when he went with Basie and them. Then Basie and them went down to Little Rock, Arkansas, and then Fletcher Henderson sent for him.
I'll read the rest of this from Chilton, and you can add. "In early 1934, left Kansas City with a band organized by
Count Basie, whilst playing in Little Rock, Arkansas, was offered a permanent job with Fletcher Henderson's band."
"Joined Henderson in Detroit, 31st of March 1934, playing in the place vacated by Coleman Hawkins. Traveled to New York with Henderson, but left the band in mid-July 1934."
"Worked with Andy Kirk in Kansas City, then played residency with Boyd Atkins in Minneapolis (late 1934). Subsequently worked with Rook Ganz..."

"...in Minneapolis, then moved back to Kansas City, gigged in various clubs, including the Sunset and the Subway. During 1936 unsuccessfully auditioned for Earl Hines' Big Band. In 1936, joined Count Basie at the Reno Club, Kansas City. Left Kansas City with Basie, and made recording debut in October 1936." So we'll stop there, and then you can pick up where you left off about him joining the band, the King Oliver group.
